react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics dataset exhibits a striking cross-paradigm convergence on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. Three independent enrichment methods — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 9.58e-15, KEGG:map00380), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p 1.59e-08, KEGG:hsa00380), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p 8.40e-05, MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) — all rank tryptophan metabolism at position 0 with 6–7 overlapping input metabolites. The driver set spans the full canonical trunk of the pathway: L-tryptophan (C00078, CHEBI:16828) as the primary substrate, with downstream products indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), tryptamine (C00398), serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598), plus the kynurenine-branch shunt intermediate 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). RaMP additionally highlights the downstream specialised modules Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550), both with FDR < 1e-07. Acrolein (C01471), doxycycline (C06973) and milrinone (C07224) did not map to any tryptophan pathway in any tool, indicating they belong to distinct biological processes or reflect off-target drug effects. A namespace discrepancy was resolved: KEGG:C00127 maps to glutathione disulfide (CHEBI:17858) rather than the hypothesised cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate. The consistent enrichment across ORA, network-diffusion (m/z) and KEGG-specific paradigms provides robust evidence that the treatment strongly dysregulates tryptophan catabolism, simultaneously elevating or depleting intermediates along both the serotonin/melatonin neuroendocrine axis and the 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid kynurenine branch — a pattern consistent with neuroinflammatory or antibiotic-mediated perturbations of gut-brain tryptophan signalling.

RaMP multi-database ORA reports KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 0 with FDR 9.58e-15 and six overlapping metabolites: L-tryptophan, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indol-3-ylacetaldehyde, tryptamine, serotonin, and melatonin. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returns the same KEGG:hsa00380 as its top hit with p-value 1.59e-08, confirming the result through a second statistical lens. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis, which operates on empirical-compound m/z matching rather than annotated IDs, returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its top pathway with p-value 8.40e-05, providing a third independent paradigm. The convergence of an ORA hypergeometric result, a second independent ORA p-value, and a network-diffusion m/z result across three separate statistical frameworks provides robust tripartite evidence that tryptophan metabolism is the primary affected pathway.

  "narrative_text": "The metabolomics dataset exhibits a striking cross-paradigm convergence on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. Three independent enrichment methods — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 9.58e-15, KEGG:map00380), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p 1.59e-08, KEGG:hsa00380), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p 8.40e-05, MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) — all rank tryptophan metabolism at position 0 with 6–7 overlapping input metabolites. The driver set spans the full canonical trunk of the pathway: L-tryptophan (C00078, CHEBI:16828) as the primary substrate, with downstream products indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), tryptamine (C00398), serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598), plus the kynurenine-branch shunt intermediate 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). RaMP additionally highlights the downstream specialised modules Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550), both with FDR < 1e-07. Acrolein (C01471), doxycycline (C06973) and milrinone (C07224) did not map to any tryptophan pathway in any tool, indicating they belong to distinct biological processes or reflect off-target drug effects. A namespace discrepancy was resolved: KEGG:C00127 maps to glutathione disulfide (CHEBI:17858) rather than the hypothesised cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics dataset exhibits a striking cross-paradigm convergence on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. Three independent enrichment methods — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 9.58e-15, KEGG:map00380), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p 1.59e-08, KEGG:hsa00380), and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p 8.40e-05, MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) — all rank tryptophan metabolism at position 0 with 6–7 overlapping input metabolites. The driver set spans the full canonical trunk of the pathway: L-tryptophan (C00078, CHEBI:16828) as the primary substrate, with downstream products indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), tryptamine (C00398), serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598), plus the kynurenine-branch shunt intermediate 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). RaMP additionally highlights the downstream specialised modules Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550), both with FDR < 1e-07. Acrolein (C01471), doxycycline (C06973) and milrinone (C07224) did not map to any tryptophan pathway in any tool, indicating they belong to distinct biological processes or reflect off-target drug effects. A namespace discrepancy was resolved: KEGG:C00127 maps to glutathione disulfide (CHEBI:17858) rather than the hypothesised cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate. The consistent enrichment across ORA, network-diffusion (m/z) and KEGG-specific paradigms provides robust evidence that the treatment strongly dysregulates tryptophan catabolism, simultaneously elevating or depleting intermediates along both the serotonin/melatonin neuroendocrine axis and the 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid kynurenine branch — a pattern consistent with neuroinflammatory or antibiotic-mediated perturbations of gut-brain tryptophan signalling.
